answer: In a fieldwork market, agents mapping juniper groves or testing nectar at zenith must lock one service permit per job. Permits are scarce, time-limited rights auctioned before job details appear; the ledger blocks simultaneous claims on one permit and releases it after delivery or forfeiture. A hundred aliases gain no extra slots unless the attacker buys or rents a hundred permits, imposing capital cost and delay. Wealthy operators could corner permits, so reserve some by lottery and cap holdings linked to one funding source.
